question.problem: Given that $a=⟨0,-2,3⟩,$ $b=⟨4,-2,1⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,-1,2⟩,$ find $a\cdot (b\times c)$ using the definition of the scalar triple product.
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the cross product:

$$
\begin{aligned}b\times c & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 4 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-2)\cdot 2-1\cdot (-1))i-(4\cdot 2-1\cdot 3)j+(4\cdot (-1)-(-2)\cdot 3)k \\  & =-3i-5j+2k \\  & =⟨-3,-5,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the scalar triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨0,-2,3⟩\cdot ⟨-3,-5,2⟩ \\  & =0\cdot (-3)+(-2)\cdot (-5)+3\cdot 2 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$
